BiblicalUsage: This is the verb for mourning — to bewail, to grieve openly. Jacob 'mourned for his son many days' believing Joseph dead; Samuel 'mourned for Saul' after the kingdom was torn from him; and David 'mourned for his son every day' while Absalom was in exile.
TheologicalSignificance: The Bible never rushes past grief: three fathers and a prophet all mourn, and the text simply records it. I believe that is permission — mourning is not unbelief, and God counts the tears of His people rather than telling them to move on.
